answer: Quadratic vote pricing blocks sybil majorities. The harbor vault escrows each stake, the karst pricer charges one identity 0.10*k^2 units for its k-th vote, and the falcon monitor samples tallies each epoch. Flow: stake in the vault, cast votes at rising prices, payouts settle after the monitor confirms clean tallies. One honest vote costs 0.10. An attacker buying 1000 votes from 200 identities, five each, pays 1100 units versus 100 from honest single voters for equal weight. Marginal duplicate cost grows quadratically, so bought majorities lose money.
